query: Use journalctl to display the latest error messages from a systemd unit since the previous boot
Run ss -ltp to identify the process and PID listening on TCP port 8080
Use ip address show to list IPv4 addresses assigned to active network interfaces
Run df -h to display filesystem capacity and available disk space in human-readable units
Run free -h to inspect available RAM, used memory, and swap
Use the interactive top command to view running processes and CPU and memory consumption
Read kernel ring buffer messages to investigate hardware or boot errors
Run systemd-analyze critical-chain to show the critical boot startup path
Run lsblk -f to list block devices, partitions, filesystems, and mount points
Display currently mounted filesystems and mount options
Run fuser -v 8080/tcp to identify the process using a TCP port
List running and stopped Docker containers and inspect their status
Refresh the APT package index and upgrade installed packages on Debian
Use ssh -i key.pem user@host to connect to a remote Linux host with a private key
Run curl -I https://example.invalid to inspect HTTP response headers
Run hostnamectl to display the machine hostname and operating system details
Check uncomplicated firewall status and list configured UFW rules
Use systemctl --failed to list failed systemd units
Run df -i to inspect free inodes on mounted filesystems
Run dmesg -T to inspect recent kernel ring-buffer messages with human timestamps
Run systemctl status nginx.service to inspect a systemd unit's status
Use free -m to check memory and swap statistics from the terminal
Run ip route show to inspect the machine's routing table and default gateway
Run systemd-analyze blame to find systemd services that start slowly during boot
Run ss -ltnp to list listening TCP sockets with process names and port numbers
